Rozdil Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Lviv Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Rozdil was home to two notable Hasidic courts — one founded by Yehuda-Zvi Eichenstein in the early 19th century, another by Pinhos-Haim Taub in 1886 — reflecting a community that by 1880 made up over half the town's population. That population declined through the interwar years to about 1,900 by 1931; Nazi occupation from June 1941 led to the deportation of roughly 1,000 Jews to the Belzec extermination camp in September 1942, with another 150 murdered in February 1943. The cemetery itself, first marked on an 1850 map, is presumed to have operated until WWII.
